packet.headline_seed: Palestinian baby shot dead by Israeli troops in occupied West Bank
packet.description_seed: The seven-month-old, Sam Fahd Abu Haikal, was in his mother’s arms when soldiers fired on family in Hebron Israeli troops killed a seven-month-old Palestinian baby in the occupied West Bank and injured one of the child’s parents after opening fire on the family’s car, despite it having complied with an order to stop. Soldiers opened fire on Friday on a car carrying the infant and his parents in the Tel Rumeida area of Hebron. The seven-month-old, Sam Fahd Abu Haikal, was critically injured, evacuated in critical condition to a hospital, where he later died. His parents were also injured. Continue reading...

The seven-month-old, Sam Fahd Abu Haikal, was in his mother’s arms when soldiers fired on family in Hebron Israeli troops killed a seven-month-old Palestinian baby in the occupied West Bank and injured one of the child’s parents after opening fire on the family’s car, despite it having complied with an order to stop. Soldiers opened fire on Friday on a car carrying the infant and his parents in the Tel Rumeida area of Hebron. The seven-month-old, Sam Fahd Abu Haikal, was critically injured, evacuated in critical condition to a hospital, where he later died. His parents were also injured. The Israeli military said troops had fired at a vehicle they believed was moving towards them, but an initial inquiry found those injured were uninvolved civilians.

Israeli troops killed a seven-month-old Palestinian baby boy after firing at his parents' vehicle in the occupied West Bank, the Palestinian health ministry said. Sam Fahd Abu Haikal was killed Friday evening, and his parents were wounded while driving in the Tel Rumeida area south of Hebron City, according to the ministry. The official Palestinian news agency WAFA said the baby was critically wounded after being struck in the face by the same bullet that injured his mother. He later died of his injuries. His father, Fahd Abu Haikal, a lecturer at Bethlehem University, was shot in the hand. They were traveling from Bethlehem to visit family in Hebron when soldiers opened fire, the agency reported.

In an interview with Israeli newspaper Haaretz, the father, Fahd Abu Haikal, a lecturer at Bethlehem University, said that “a bullet passed through his hand and struck his son, Sam, who was being held by his mother in the back seat”. Abu Haikal said the family, which also included the couple’s 11-year-old son and Abu Haikal’s mother, had been driving through Hebron on Friday evening when soldiers signalled for the vehicle to stop, he said. He said it was still daylight and that the soldier who opened fire could clearly see the occupants were a family. “The soldier signalled me to stop. I brought the car to a complete halt and raised my hands on the steering wheel. Immediately afterwards, they opened fire on the vehicle,” he told Haaretz.

The seven-month-old, Sam Fahd Abu Haikal, was in his mother’s arms when soldiers fired on family in Hebron

Israeli troops killed a seven-month-old Palestinian baby in the occupied West Bank and injured one of the child’s parents after opening fire on the family’s car, despite it having complied with an order to stop.

Soldiers opened fire on Friday on a car carrying the infant and his parents in the Tel Rumeida area of Hebron. The seven-month-old, Sam Fahd Abu Haikal, was critically injured, evacuated in critical condition to a hospital, where he later died. His parents were also injured.

The Israeli military said troops had fired at a vehicle they believed was moving towards them, but an initial inquiry found those injured were uninvolved civilians.

In an interview with Israeli newspaper Haaretz, the father, Fahd Abu Haikal, a lecturer at Bethlehem University, said that “a bullet passed through his hand and struck his son, Sam, who was being held by his mother in the back seat”. Abu Haikal said the family, which also included the couple’s 11-year-old son and Abu Haikal’s mother, had been driving through Hebron on Friday evening when soldiers signalled for the vehicle to stop, he said.

He said it was still daylight and that the soldier who opened fire could clearly see the occupants were a family. “The soldier signalled me to stop. I brought the car to a complete halt and raised my hands on the steering wheel. Immediately afterwards, they opened fire on the vehicle,” he told Haaretz.

The Israel Defense Forces said its troops “perceived a vehicle accelerating toward them” and one of the soldiers “responded with single shots toward the vehicle”.

“As a result, three Palestinians were injured and evacuated for medical treatment,” the IDF said, adding that “the incident is under review” and expressed “deep sorrow for any harm caused to uninvolved individuals”.

Abu Haikal rejected the military’s account.

“The soldier was about 10 metres away from me. He saw me, he saw my wife and the children,” he told Haaretz. ‘‘The windows were not tinted, it was broad daylight and everything was clear. You can’t say he didn’t see that it was a family.

“I stopped as I was instructed to, and then they simply shot at the car,” he added. “There was no clear checkpoint, just soldiers standing in the street. I stopped when I was asked to, and then the shooting started,” he said.

Israeli troops killed a seven-month-old Palestinian baby boy after firing at his parents' vehicle in the occupied West Bank, the Palestinian health ministry said.

Sam Fahd Abu Haikal was killed Friday evening, and his parents were wounded while driving in the Tel Rumeida area south of Hebron City, according to the ministry.

The official Palestinian news agency WAFA said the baby was critically wounded after being struck in the face by the same bullet that injured his mother. He later died of his injuries. His father, Fahd Abu Haikal, a lecturer at Bethlehem University, was shot in the hand. They were traveling from Bethlehem to visit family in Hebron when soldiers opened fire, the agency reported.

Photos from the Associated Press show that the baby's carseat was behind the driver's seat of the vehicle. Photos also show damage, including at least one bullet hole, in the car's windshield.

Israel's military has scaled up military operations in the West Bank since the Oct. 7, 2023 Hamas attack that killed some 1,200 people and took 251 people hostage, which triggered the war in Gaza. Israel's retaliatory military campaign has so far killed more than 72,900 Palestinians, according to Gaza's Health Ministry. The ministry, which is part of the Hamas-led government, is generally seen as reliable by United Nations agencies and independent experts.

A spokesperson for the Israel Defense Forces told CBS News that soldiers "perceived a vehicle accelerating toward them" in the Hebron area. A soldier responded by firing single shots, the spokesperson said. The statement said three Palestinians were injured and evacuated for medical treatment, but did not confirm the age or gender of any of the injured.

An initial inquiry "found that those injured were uninvolved civilians," the IDF spokesperson said, adding that the incident is under review and that the IDF "expresses deep sorrow for any harm caused to uninvolved individuals."

payload.title: Vauva kuoli Israelin sotilaiden tulituksessa Hebronissa
payload.summary: Seitsemän kuukauden ikäinen Sam Fahd Abu Haikal kuoli haavoituttuaan Israelin sotilaiden tulituksessa miehitetyllä Länsirannalla. Perhe oli autolla Hebronin Tel Rumeidan alueella perjantai-iltana, kun sotilaat avasivat tulen.
payload.content:
Seitsemän kuukauden ikäinen palestiinalaisvauva Sam Fahd Abu Haikal on kuollut sen jälkeen, kun Israelin sotilaat avasivat tulen hänen perheensä autoon miehitetyllä Länsirannalla. Tapaus sattui perjantai-iltana Hebronin Tel Rumeidan alueella, kun lapsi oli lähdetietojen mukaan äitinsä sylissä auton takapenkillä. Hänet vietiin sairaalaan kriittisessä tilassa, mutta hän kuoli myöhemmin vammoihinsa.

## Perhe oli matkalla Hebroniin

Palestiinalaisten terveysviranomaisten mukaan vauva kuoli sen jälkeen, kun sotilaat ampuivat hänen vanhempiensa ajoneuvoa. Myös lapsen vanhemmat haavoittuivat. Palestiinalaisen WAFA-uutistoimiston mukaan perhe oli matkalla Betlehemistä Hebroniin tapaamaan sukulaisia.

WAFA:n mukaan lapsi haavoittui vakavasti kasvoihin samasta luodista, joka haavoitti hänen äitiään. Isä Fahd Abu Haikal, joka työskentelee luennoitsijana Betlehemin yliopistossa, haavoittui käteen. Isä kertoi israelilaislehti Haaretzille, että luoti kulki hänen kätensä läpi ja osui hänen poikaansa, jota äiti piteli takapenkillä.

## Isän mukaan auto oli pysähtynyt

Haaretzille antamassaan kuvauksessa Fahd Abu Haikal sanoi, että autossa olivat myös pariskunnan 11-vuotias poika ja Abu Haikalin äiti. Hänen mukaansa perhe ajoi Hebronissa perjantai-iltana, kun sotilaat viittoivat ajoneuvoa pysähtymään.

Fahd Abu Haikalin mukaan hän pysäytti auton kokonaan ja nosti kätensä ratille ennen tulitusta. Hän sanoi, että oli yhä valoisaa ja että tulen avanneen sotilaan olisi pitänyt nähdä autossa olleen perhe.

## Armeija kertoo alustavasta selvityksestä

Israelin armeija on sanonut, että sotilaat ampuivat ajoneuvoa, jonka he uskoivat liikkuvan heitä kohti. Armeijan mukaan alustavassa selvityksessä todettiin kuitenkin, että haavoittuneet olivat sivullisia siviilejä.

Saatavilla olevien tietojen perusteella Sam Fahd Abu Haikal haavoittui tulituksessa perjantai-iltana, kuljetettiin sairaalaan kriittisessä tilassa ja kuoli myöhemmin vammoihinsa. Tapaus sattui Tel Rumeidan alueella Hebronissa, miehitetyllä Länsirannalla.

Myös lapsen vanhemmat haavoittuivat perheen autoon kohdistuneessa tulituksessa.
Israelin armeijan mukaan alustava selvitys viittaa siihen, että haavoittuneet olivat sivullisia siviilejä.
